meaning: If part p of a nonempty-family least upper bound overlaps no selected member, exact complementation supplies a remainder containing every selected member. Leastness puts the whole inside that remainder, contradicting reflexive overlap of p. Conversely, the no-extra-parts clause supplies overlap inclusion into any upper bound; import the existing separationCharacterization theorem with strong supplementation derived from complementation to obtain containment. The nonempty guard is explicit; neither atomism nor all-family formation is needed.
